articles.headline: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels suffers elbow injury against Cowboys
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field in Sunday's game against the Cowboys after suffering an injured left elbow on the final play of the first half.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys after suffering an injured left elbow on the final play of the first half.

He was ruled out for the rest of the game. 

Daniels' feet appeared to get stepped on by left guard Chris Paul as he took the snap on a third-and-goal from the 1-yard line. Daniels started to fall down and tried to brace himself with his left elbow, which then bent back.

Daniels flung a pass attempt and stayed on the ground. He got up, started to run off the field then went back down to the ground. He was looked at by medical personnel and surrounded by a number of teammates as well as coaches, including Dan Quinn. As he was carted off, Daniels sat up with a towel over his head.

Daniels had dislocated his left elbow last season in Week 9 against Seattle. He returned four weeks later but re-injured the elbow attempting to make a tackle following an interception in Week 14 at Minnesota. He did not play the rest of the season.

Sunday, Daniels had led the Commanders back from a 17-3 deficit by throwing a touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs and then leading them on a drive to end the first half. Washington decided to go for it on third and goal rather than kick a field goal with three seconds left.

Daniels completed 11 of 17 passes for 96 yards but hurt the Cowboys on the ground as well, resembling the player who was named the NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Daniels had rushed seven times for 69 yards on Sunday.

articles.headline: Anderson tosses 7 shutout innings, Mariners beat Rockies 2-1 to avoid elimination
articles.description: — Rookie Kade Anderson tossed seven shutout innings, Dominic Canzone drove in two runs, and the Seattle Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday to stave off elimination from playoff contention.
articles.body:
DENVER -- — Rookie Kade Anderson tossed seven shutout innings, Dominic Canzone drove in two runs, and the Seattle Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday to stave off elimination from playoff contention.


              Anderson (2-2), in the longest of his six starts since making his major league debut Aug. 22 at the Chicago Cubs, followed his worst outing with his best. He gave up three hits, struck out a career-high seven and didn’t walk a batter.


              His performance kept Seattle’s slim postseason hopes alive. The Mariners (73-83) gained a game on Texas in the AL West and avoided, temporarily, being eliminated from the AL wild-card race.


              Mariners closer Andrés Muñoz left the game after walking TJ Rumfield with one out in the ninth. Muñoz bent over flexing his right arm after missing on a 98 mph fastball, bringing out the trainer. Manager Dan Wilson said Munoz’s issue was with his right knee He was replaced by Eduard Bazardo, who got the final two outs around a walk for his first save.


              Colorado catcher Hunter Goodman hit his 39th homer off Muñoz.


              Rockies starter Tomoyuki Sugano, who entered Sunday with a 7.41 ERA in three September starts, set down the first 10 batters before running into trouble in the fourth. He walked Randy Arozarena, and he scored from first on Canzone’s single to center.


              Canzone gave Seattle a 2-0 lead with an RBI double in the sixth off of Ryan Feltner.


              Colorado’s best scoring opportunity against Anderson was in the sixth inning when Jake McCarthy tripled with one out. Anderson got Connor Norby looking for the second out and struck out Goodman to end the inning.


              Rockies third baseman Kyle Karros was a late scratch with back spasms.


              Up next
              Mariners: RHP Logan Gilbert (12-10, 3.69 ERA) faces the Astros on Tuesday night to open the season-ending homestand.


              Rockies: LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38) opens the final home series against the Diamondbacks on Tuesday night.

articles.headline: Panthers in awe of LB Devin Lloyd's 'dominant' game on defense
articles.description: Devin Lloyd finished Sunday's win over the Falcons with two interceptions, including one for a pick-six, nine total tackles, a sack and three pass breakups.
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he'd never before seen a linebacker take over a game like Devin Lloyd did in the third quarter of Sunday's 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Lloyd had two interceptions, including one for a pick-six, nine total tackles, a sack and three pass breakups.

"I don't know if I've seen a better performance out of a linebacker in 17 years of coaching in the NFL," Canales said after the road win.

In the locker room, Lloyd's teammates were also in awe. The team captain, who was signed to a three-year, $45 million free agent deal in March, singlehandedly outscored the Falcons, 6-3.

"That's probably the most dominant performance I've seen ... from a defensive player since I've been here," two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Jaycee Horn said.

 

"He better win [NFC] Defensive Player of the Week," defensive end Derrick Brown said with a smile.

Lloyd had five interceptions last season during his final year with the Jacksonville Jaguars. After watching the Panthers allow 59 points and 552 yards in their home-opening loss to the Chicago Bears, Lloyd took it upon himself to be a gamechanger.

Along with producing two interceptions of his own, his other pass breakup set up an interception for fellow inside linebacker Bobby Okereke.

"The biggest thing is just us coming out with the win," Lloyd said. "Just grateful for the team -- we played great complementary football. We found a way to respond from last week and come out with the victory."

Lloyd helped seal that victory before the end of the third quarter.

With 3:08 left in the frame, rookie quarterback Jack Strand -- filling in for Cooper Rush, who was benched after Lloyd's first third-quarter interception -- threw a pass to wideout Jahan Dotson. The pass was broken up by Horn and the ball landed in Lloyd's hands around the 16-yard line.

From there, Lloyd was off to the races to pay dirt.

Running back Chuba Hubbard called it a "Madden moment" before anointing Lloyd as a "one-of-one player."

Lloyd admitted after the game that he knew he'd score on the second interception.

"As soon as I got it, and then I made one [defender] miss, then I knew I was just going to fall into the end zone," Lloyd said.

The Panthers' defense held the Falcons' offense to 286 net yards and three total points. Carolina also had five total takeaways, with Lloyd involved in at least three of them.

"One of the most dominant linebacker performances I've seen," Canales said.

articles.headlineJa: 月曜日のファンタジーベースボール・ラインナップ助言：ベイリー・オーバーを信頼できるか？
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日のMLBの試合に向けてファンタジーベースボールのラインナップを組むために必要なすべての情報。
articles.body:
Check out all of our starting pitcher rankings and other lineup selection tools here to help you make smart fantasy baseball lineup decisions. All fantasy advice is geared toward ESPN 10-team leagues with standard scoring.

Note: All information is accurate as of the time of publication. For updates, as well as any breaking news that might impact today's MLB slate, be sure to check out the latest fantasy baseball buzz. 

Other resources: RP depth chart | 2026 Rankings

ESPN's 2026 Player Rater | Betting notes for Monday

Pitchers to stream on Monday

Bailey Ober has walked an inordinately high number of hitters down the stretch. It's not the ideal setup for a streamer, but the Minnesota Twins have a road date with the San Francisco Giants so the veteran right-hander faces a depleted lineup in a pitcher's haven. The Giants will be without Rafael Devers for the rest of the season and may not have Bryce Eldridge come out of concussion protocol by game time.

Shane Baz left his last start after being struck on the elbow by a 105-mph line drive. He made it through the week unscathed, so he'll start for the Baltimore Orioles in the opener of a home series with the Toronto Blue Jays. On a busier slate, Baz would not make the cut, but there are only three games from which to choose, and the Blue Jays have struggled on the road facing right-handers all season.

Keider Montero will serve as the Detroit Tigers' primary pitcher when they host the Washington Nationals. River Ryan is set to make his Tigers debut, but he's probably earmarked for two or three frames before passing the baton to Montero. It should be a productive evening for the Tigers offense, giving Montero the chance for a win. He's had a couple of missteps over the past two months, but Montero has generally exhibited solid command and control this season, compensating for a low strikeout rate.

Hitters to stream on Monday

The Tigers' right-handed contingent lines up for a productive evening at Comerica Park with a matchup against Nationals lefty Jackson Kent. The southpaw sports a 6.40 ERA and 1.76 WHIP, fanning only 27 while walking a generous 23 in just 32 1/3 frames. Gleyber Torres, Hao-Yu Lee, Spencer Torkelson and John Peck enjoy the platoon advantage.

Brett Bateman hasn't compiled many homers and steals, but he gets on base and scores runs for the Toronto Blue Jays. He'll likely hit leadoff and enjoy the platoon edge with Shane Baz on the hill.

Walker Jenkins will be one of the favorites for next season's AL Rookie of the Year. The Twins are giving him a look down the stretch, and even though he's only hitting .211 through Saturday's action, he has clubbed three homers and a steal in his inaugural 18 games. The 21-year-old left-handed batter faces the San Francisco Giants' Landen Roupp. The right-hander sports a 1.77 ERA over his last four outings, but in 20 1/3 innings, he fanned only 13 while allowing a bloated 11 walks.

articles.headline: QB Kyler Murray (concussion) expected to return for Week 3
articles.description: The Vikings should have QB Kyler Murray available to them next week. Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol "pretty early in the week," coach Kevin O'Connell said.
articles.headlineJa: QBカイラー・マレー（脳震盪）は第3週に復帰の見込み
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスは来週、QBカイラー・マレーを起用できる見通しだ。ケビン・オコンネル監督によると、マレーは「週のかなり早い段階で」脳震盪プロトコルをクリアする見込みだという。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- After starting the season 2-0 behind backup quarterback Carson Wentz, the Minnesota Vikings should have starter Kyler Murray available to them next week. Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol "pretty early in the week," coach Kevin O'Connell said Sunday after the Vikings' 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears.

O'Connell did not announce that Murray would be the starter for the Vikings' next game, Sept. 27 at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but that has been the assumption around the team after Murray participated in all three practices last week on a limited basis.

"He's doing great," O'Connell said. "He's feeling well."

Murray suffered his concussion on the 11th play of his debut game with the Vikings last week, but his symptoms were minor enough to allow him to practice. Wentz has completed 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns since replacing Murray, without committing a turnover, and he made two throws in the fourth quarter Sunday that helped the Vikings drain clock while protecting a one-score lead.

Wentz hit receiver Jordan Addison on a 15-yard pass over the middle to convert a third down and later threw a 19-yard floater to tight end T.J. Hockenson on 2nd-and-10. Those completions helped the Vikings run 5 minutes, 8 seconds off the clock before taking a 6-point lead on Will Reichard's 39-yard field goal.

"It was ugly out there," Wentz said. "I'm not going to lie. But I'd rather win ugly than look good and come up with an 'L.'"

But there has never been any indication that Wentz has been playing his way into a full-time starting job. The Vikings' offense has finished with less than 300 total yards in both games this season, and Wentz has taken six sacks and had one interception overturned by a penalty. He had another likely interception dropped in Sunday's rainy conditions at Soldier Field.

articles.headline: 49ers lose another WR as Demarcus Robinson suffers ankle injury
articles.description: Demarcus Robinson departed late in the second quarter of Sunday's matchup with the Miami Dolphins.
articles.headlineJa: 49ers、デマルカス・ロビンソンの足首負傷でまたもWRを失う
articles.descriptionJa: デマルカス・ロビンソンは、日曜日のマイアミ・ドルフィンズ戦の第2クォーター終盤に負傷退場した。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- For the second time in as many games, the San Francisco 49ers lost a wide receiver to an ankle injury, as Demarcus Robinson departed late in the second quarter of Sunday's matchup with the Miami Dolphins.

After rookie De'Zhaun Stribling suffered a left ankle injury that required surgery and will keep him out 10 weeks last week against the Los Angeles Rams, Robinson came up limping after a 20-yard catch with 6:46 to go in the second quarter on Sunday.

On the play, Robinson came open on the left hash as quarterback Brock Purdy led him a bit too far. Robinson extended for the ball and rolled over as he secured the catch. He attempted to get back up to score but was unable to get up and a Dolphins defender touched him down.

Robinson favored his right ankle as he quickly hobbled to the medical tent on the Niners' sideline. A few moments later, a cart arrived and took Robinson to the locker room.

The 49ers initially designated Robinson as questionable to return but the team ruled him out at halftime. Absent Stribling, the Niners had been using Robinson and Deebo Samuel to help fill the void with Samuel starting Sunday and Robinson rotating in.

Robinson had three catches for 35 yards when he went out. Without Robinson, the only Niners receivers available are Mike Evans, Samuel, Jacob Cowing and KhaDarel Hodge. Ricky Pearsall is out for the year following knee surgery and veteran Christian Kirk is on injured reserve with a calf issue.

articles.headline: Gavin Williams dominates with 7 shutout frames as Guardians edge Athletics to stay atop AL Central
articles.description: — Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the AL Central.
articles.headlineJa: ギャビン・ウィリアムズが7回無失点と圧倒、ガーディアンズがアスレチックスを下しア・リーグ中地区首位をキープ
articles.descriptionJa: ギャビン・ウィリアムズが7回無失点の好投を見せ、ジョー・アデルのタイムリー内野安打もあり、クリーブランド・ガーディアンズは日曜日、アスレチックスを1-0で破ってア・リーグ中地区首位を守った。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- — Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the AL Central.


              Steven Kwan added three hits for Cleveland, which posted its seventh series sweep of the season and third at home.


              The Guardians (81-75) are 1 1/2 games in front of the Chicago White Sox. They finish the season on the road with series against Boston and Kansas City. 


              Williams (14-8) gave up three hits and struck out nine to move into the major-league lead with 244 strikeouts. He has one more than Milwaukee’s Jacob Misiorowski. Toronto’s Dylan Cease is in third with 239. It is the 13th time in 31 starts this season that the right-hander has had at least nine strikeouts.


              Cade Smith worked 1 1/3 innings for his 39th save in 44 opportunities.


              The Athletics were swept for the second straight series and lost all six games on their road trip.


              José Ramírez led off the fourth with a double down the right-field line, advanced to third on Chase DeLauter's fly out to left and scored on Jo Adell's infield single. Pitcher Jack Perkins (3-12) fielded the soft grounder on the grass in front of the mound, but his throw hit Adell in the back as he was in the basepath.


              Athletics manager Mark Kotsay was ejected for the third time this season for agruing the call. 


              Perkins went six innings and allowed one run on four hits. 


              The Athletics' best chance came in the eighth inning when they had runners on second and third with one out. Hunter Gaddis struck out pinch-hitter Carlos Cortes and Smith whiffed Henry Bolte.


              Up next
              Athletics: Return home to face the Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday. LHP Brady Brasso (1-3, 4.50 ERA) will take the mound.


              Guardians: LHP Parker Messic (12-9, 2.57 ERA) goes on Tuesday to start a three-game series at Boston.

articles.headline: Eagles' Broadway jab at Titans leads NFL Week 2 trolls
articles.description: Teams across the NFL came with petty postgame energy after wins in Week 2, led by the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルスのタイタンズへのブロードウェイでの煽りがNFL第2週の挑発合戦をリード
articles.descriptionJa: フィラデルフィア・イーグルスを筆頭に、NFLの各チームが第2週の勝利後に冷やかしや煽り合いを展開した。
articles.body:
With half the league looking to remain undefeated heading into Week 2, a win could lead to an even sweeter troll. Case in point? The Philadelphia Eagles.

The Eagles utilized a late two-minute drive to steal a 24-20 win against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville.

Tennessee took a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left and needed one stop for its first win of the season. However, Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts led his team down the field with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Darius Cooper with nine seconds left. It marked the Eagles' latest game-winning passing touchdown since 2012, according to ESPN Research.

Nashville is home to the famous Broadway Street, but Philadelphia has its own notable street too: "Broad Street." Therefore, the Eagles posted a graphic of an Eagle on a "Broadway" street sign but covered "way" with a sticky note that read: "Street," putting a spin on Nashville's area.

Here are more of the top trolls from NFL Week 2.

Carolina Panthers 34, Atlanta Falcons 3

Carolina defeated its NFC South foe on the road Sunday in convincing fashion.

Panthers quarterback Bryce Young passed for 287 yards and three touchdowns, two of which went to tight end Darren Waller. Carolina forced five turnovers -- three interceptions and two fumbles -- as Atlanta had just 286 total yards of offense.

Carolina's blowout win came with an equally dominant social media performance. It first shared a victory post with the score and caption: "Feelin' Peachy," a reference to Georgia being known as the Peach State. The Panthers then posted a graphic of a Panther eating a bird's egg with the caption: "We cooked."

New Orleans Saints 24, Baltimore Ravens 17

The Saints faced a 17-9 deficit heading into the fourth quarter, but responded with consecutive touchdowns -- the final one coming with 1:28 left in the game. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw an interception on the ensuing drive, and New Orleans secured the victory.

The NFC South team directed its troll toward an unlikely source: a Baltimore fan who had choice words for Saints fans on X. They wrote that Saints fans were "talking crazier than Colts fans," the Ravens' Week 1 opponents, and they'd similarly learn the "hard way" like Indianapolis' followers. Baltimore defeated Indianapolis last Sunday.

New Orleans remembered the slight, quoting the post with a video of wide receiver Chris Olave celebrating his fourth-quarter touchdown with the caption: "Love those crazy Saints fans."

Minnesota Vikings 9, Chicago Bears 3

Another divisional game brought another troll, this time from the Minnesota Vikings.

Minnesota kept Chicago in check after the Bears put up 59 points in a Week 1 victory. The Vikings forced two turnovers, including one as Chicago running back D'Andre Swift fumbled while diving for a touchdown. The Bears reached the red zone again, but had a field goal blocked with 6:23 left in the game. Minnesota got one more stop to claim the win.

T
